brief: A planter for a sunny kitchen windowsill with three herbs growing in it.

requirements.evidence: 3 full hex bases in a row (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:2,0,0;full) with hex-bin-full bins; compact linear footprint suits a sill; meshClash clear.
requirements.requirement: Planter for a kitchen windowsill (compact, sill-sized)

requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,0 basil-young, bin:1,0,0 mint-young, bin:2,0,0 parsley-young, each in soil via fill_and_plant; visible in look views.
Build is a small row planter that can sit on a sunny sill, but sunlight, watering and food/material safety depend on user-chosen print material and placement, which the configurator does not check.

finish.summary: Built a 3-cell linear planter (3 full bases + 3 full-depth bins) with soil and three young herbs: basil, mint and flat-leaf parsley. House rules applied, meshClash clear, all plants visible from front and top views.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
